text: Four and a half thousand years ago, while Egypt built its pyramids, a city on the Indus had drains under every street.
This is Mohenjo-daro. With Harappa, it was the heart of the Indus Valley Civilisation.
Streets ran in a grid. Bricks were baked to the same proportions. Most homes had their own bathroom.
Merchants stamped their goods with seals, in a script no one can read, to this day.
Around nineteen hundred B C E, the rivers shifted, the monsoon weakened, and the cities emptied.
asr: Around 1900 BCE, the rivers shifted, the monsoon weakened, and the cities emptied.

text: Four thousand years later, archaeologists dug into a mound called Mohenjo-daro. The Mound of the Dead.
